studies.claim: Across 15 studies, each additional weekly set per muscle was associated with a 0.37% increase in muscle size, and 10+ weekly sets beat fewer than 5.
studies.population: 390 mostly young untrained and recreationally trained men
studies.effect: +0.37% muscle size per weekly set; ES difference 0.24 for 10+ vs <5 sets
studies.snippet: Each additional weekly set per muscle was associated with a 0.37% increase in muscle size.

studies.claim: Hypertrophy kept increasing with weekly sets but with diminishing returns per set.
studies.effect: marginal gain per set roughly halved between 10 and 20 sets
studies.snippet: hypertrophy increased with weekly sets with diminishing returns; the marginal gain per set fell by roughly half between 10 and 20 sets.

studies.claim: Frequency does not matter when volume is equated; not about total volume.
studies.snippet: With weekly volume equated, effect sizes did not differ by frequency (p=0.42).

studies.claim: In trained men, 30 weekly sets increased quadriceps thickness 6.8% versus 2.1% with 6 sets over 8 weeks.
studies.population: 34 resistance-trained men, mean training age 4.4 years
studies.snippet: The high volume group grew a lot more muscle than everyone else.

studies.claim: Protein supplementation study; not about training volume.
studies.snippet: Protein supplementation increased fat-free mass gains by 0.30 kg (95% CI 0.09 to 0.52).

studies.claim: In untrained women, 3 sets per exercise increased muscle thickness 4.9% versus 2.4% with 1 set.
studies.snippet: Muscle thickness increased 4.9% with 3 sets and 2.4% with 1 set.

studies.claim: In rats, higher ladder-climbing volume produced greater plantaris hypertrophy.
studies.snippet: Rats performing higher training volume on a weighted ladder-climbing protocol showed greater plantaris muscle hypertrophy than low-volume rats after 8 weeks.
